reviews.review: One of the best Roguelikes i've ever played. 8/8 IGN, Would Play Many Hours More.

Risk of Rain was a solid entry in the loose canon of the early “randomised indie” era, sitting comfortably alongside [i]The Binding of Isaac[/i] and [i]Dungeons of Dredmor[/i]. It wore its Cave Story influence openly, from the eerie soundtrack, to the hostile alien world, to the simple loop of pushing through semi-randomised stages before making a break for the ship. The structure was well-crafted, the stakes were obvious, and the pace was brisk enough that its derivative foundations rarely became a distraction.

Its most crucial asset was character differentiation. While some overlap existed, the variety impacted play significantly. Bandit and Commando appeared similar on paper, but area control versus knockback meaningfully changed encounter flow. HAN-D and Mercenary shared a melee focus, yet one survived through sustain and the other through mobility. Acrid and CHEF occupied stranger, more specialised spaces. Enemy design struck a pleasing balance between cute and threatening, supported by an unusually strong bestiary and item log.

Item synergies were where the game stood out. Learning how effects stacked and interacted was consistently satisfying, and runs could be short or drawn out depending on appetite and confidence. Local co-op worked cleanly with controllers, which was notable at the time and materially improved the experience.

The limitations became clear with a few loops. Early stages turned into routine after enough runs, and it was easy to reach a point where stacked items caused the challenge to dissolve, particularly on lower difficulties. Certain artifacts and drones further undermined balance. Late-game performance issues also intruded, with lag and screen tearing arriving precisely when the stakes were highest.

For solo controller play, it was an easy 7 out of 10. With a co-op partner close to your skill level, it climbed to a 9. It wasn’t perfect, but was simple fun, and sometimes that really is enough. 

I still have a print of Providence hanging on my wall - and that illustrates the minor but enduring impact Risk of Rain had on me quite nicely.
I stacked 1099 barbed wires and defeated the final boss in 2 seconds. 11/10 would become OP again.
